resource.name: aws_redshift_parameter_group
resource.description: Provides a Redshift Cluster parameter group resource.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_redshift_parameter_group` resource enables the creation and management of custom parameter groups for Amazon Redshift clusters, allowing users to configure database engine settings to optimize performance and behavior. Common use cases include fine-tuning query execution, memory allocation, and logging settings to meet specific workload requirements or compliance needs. This resource is essential for customizing cluster configurations, such as enabling query monitoring, adjusting timeout settings, or modifying encryption parameters, to align with application demands and organizational policies.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an AWS Redshift parameter group using the `aws_redshift_parameter_group` resource, including setting custom parameters such as `require_ssl`, `query_group`, and `enable_user_activity_logging`. It illustrates how to define multiple `parameter` blocks to customize Redshift cluster behavior for enhanced security, query management, and activity logging.

arguments.name: description
arguments.description: (Optional) The description of the Redshift parameter group. Defaults to "Managed by Terraform".
arguments.llm_summary: The `description` argument for the `aws_redshift_parameter_group` resource allows users to define a human-readable explanation or label for the parameter group, providing context or documentation about its purpose or configuration. Setting this argument helps users organize and identify parameter groups within their Redshift environment, especially in multi-environment or complex deployments, and defaults to "Managed by Terraform" if not specified.

arguments.name: family
arguments.description: (Required) The family of the Redshift parameter group.
arguments.llm_summary: The `family` argument specifies the Redshift engine version compatibility for the parameter group, ensuring that the group is tailored to the configuration requirements of a specific Redshift cluster version. By setting this required value, users define the foundational parameter group family, enabling the customization of database settings aligned with the selected Redshift engine version.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument represents the unique identifier of the Redshift parameter group, which is automatically generated by Terraform upon resource creation. While not configurable, it is commonly used for referencing the parameter group in other resources or outputs, enabling integration and resource tracking within the infrastructure.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the Redshift parameter.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument in the `aws_redshift_parameter_group` resource specifies the unique identifier for the Redshift parameter group, allowing users to define and manage a distinct configuration set for database parameters. By setting this argument, users establish a named grouping of custom parameter values that can be applied to Redshift clusters, enabling tailored database behavior to meet specific application or workload requirements.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level. You can read more about the parameters that Redshift supports in the documentation
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_redshift_parameter_group` resource allows users to assign metadata in the form of key-value pairs to the parameter group, enabling resource categorization, organization, and identification for purposes such as cost allocation, environment labeling, or automation workflows. When configured, it ensures consistent tagging across resources and can override provider-level default tags for enhanced control over tag management.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_redshift_parameter_group` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags (as a `map(string)`) that are applied to the parameter group and any inherited resources. This facilitates resource organization, cost allocation, and governance by enabling consistent tagging across all associated AWS resources, aligning with common practices for managing environments, ownership, or compliance.

blocks.name: parameter
blocks.description: (Optional) A list of Redshift parameters to apply.  Parameter blocks support the following:

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the Redshift parameter.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument specifies the unique identifier for the Redshift parameter group, allowing users to define and reference a custom configuration set for database parameters. By setting this value, users can manage and apply tailored parameter settings to optimize Redshift cluster behavior for specific workloads or environments.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: (Required) The value of the Redshift parameter.
arguments.llm_summary: The `value` argument specifies the desired configuration for a Redshift parameter within the `aws_redshift_parameter_group`, allowing users to define the operational behavior or performance tuning of their Redshift cluster (e.g., query optimization, memory allocation). Setting this argument directly impacts how the cluster handles specific workloads or features, aligning it with the user's performance and functionality requirements.

blocks.llm_summary: The `parameter` configuration block within the `aws_redshift_parameter_group` resource allows users to define and customize a list of Redshift database parameters, enabling fine-grained control over database behavior and performance settings. By specifying individual parameters and their values, this block helps users tailor Redshift clusters to meet specific workload requirements, optimize query execution, and enforce compliance with organizational policies.
